event.label: single head lift from phone to camera while walking
event.type: brief state transition; the new gaze persists, not a down-up nod
event.observation: Man looks down at phone before frame 43; raises gaze/head across frames 43–52, then maintains forward gaze and smiles. Walking and phone holding continue. Boundaries visual and approximate ±3 frames.

limitations: A sustained new gaze follows the short head-lift transition; this is not an event that necessarily falls entirely between 2 FPS observations.
Whole-body walking is inferred from original source and upper-body/background motion; lower legs are outside source framing.

event.label: one brief double thumbs-up gesture between larger one-arm celebratory movements
event.type: brief closed excursion; both hands rise, thumbs-up, then lower
event.observation: Both hands visible and thumbs extended next to head/chest, especially frames 52–61. Before and after, single-arm celebratory movements occur. This is not a clap. Frame boundaries approximate ±2 frames.

limitations: Source title uses animated to mean energetic, not cartoon; video is live-action.
Raised fist near the top edge in surrounding large motions was already source-framed; target thumbs-up hands are fully visible.
Fast raising/lowering shows source motion blur; score clear-gesture interval separately from transition boundaries.

event.label: one bilateral hands-to-headphone-earcups interval followed by release during dance
event.type: longer contact/near-contact control; not an ultra-short event
event.observation: At start, an individual hand is already near one ear during dance. Distinct bilateral interval begins around frame 40; both hands remain at or immediately next to the headphone earcups while the torso sways, then release/lift away across 81–91. Visual contact boundary is approximate ±4 frames; do not score millimeter fingertip contact.

limitations: This is a roughly 1.7-second bilateral hold and is deliberately a longer-event control, not a 0.3–0.7-second short event.
One hand is already near an ear at clip start; count the bilateral interval, not all individual hand-ear encounters.
Fingertip physical contact cannot be certified at all frames; primary label is bilateral hand-to-earcup pose and release.
